sections.h2: What kind of county is Laclede County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Laclede County is a rural Ozarks county in south central Missouri whose courthouse and biggest city share the name Lebanon. The land runs 765 square miles, and a slice of the Mark Twain National Forest sits inside it. Camden, Pulaski, Texas, Wright, Webster and Dallas counties form the boundary.

Missouri organized the county on February 24, 1849, and named it for Pierre Laclede, who founded St. Louis. The 2020 count was 36,039 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate stands at 36,943.

Lebanon is the only large city. Conway, Richland, Phillipsburg, Stoutland and Evergreen are the other incorporated places, and Bennett Springs is a census-designated place. Check whether your house lies inside a city limit or out on a county road before you list.

sections.h2: How is Laclede County run, and which school districts touch it?
sections.html:
Laclede County is a statutory third class county, and its government works from the Laclede County Government Center in Lebanon. The county's website says the first permanent courthouse opened in 1851, a replacement from 1894 burned in 1920, and the 1925 building cost $72,428. Voters approved a law enforcement sales tax in August 1994, and that money paid for the present center.

The same page gives a 2024 assessed valuation of $549,845,759, up from $20,234,001 in 1960. The county's population estimate there is 36,680 for 2023, and it calls the growth rapid.

Five public school districts have campuses here: Lebanon R-III, Laclede County R-I at Conway, Gasconade C-4 at Falcon, Joel E. Barber C-5 and Stoutland R-II. Whichever one serves your address places a levy on your bill, so list the district when you describe the house to a buyer.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau report about homes and incomes in Laclede County?
sections.html:
A typical owned home in Laclede County is valued at $168,400 in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, and owners live in 68.2% of homes. Household income sits at $53,282 in 2024 dollars, and 14.9% of residents are below the poverty line.

  • 14,558 households, averaging 2.48 people
  • 16,211 housing units in July 2025
  • Gross rent of $809 at the median
  • Owner costs of $1,160 a month with a mortgage and $405 without
  • A commute of 21.4 minutes on average

Owners with no mortgage have no escrow account paying the bill for them, so the statement from the collector is the only prompt to pay. If you inherited a paid-off house, put the due date on your calendar.

sections.h2: Which Laclede County office does what?
sections.html:
The Assessor decides what a parcel is worth, and the Collector of Revenue turns that value into a bill and takes the payment. The collector's site is firm about the split: the office collects from the assessor's records and cannot edit a bill. A wrong acreage, owner name or parcel description goes to the Assessor at (417) 532-7163.

The Collector's office also handles merchant license fees and railroad and utility tax, and it distributes money to schools, road districts, fire protection entities and other local subdivisions. Mortgage companies send escrow payments to the same counter.

The collector's online center lets you look up a bill by owner name, parcel number, street address or account number and see the payment history. Open your parcel before you list, so you know which years are paid.

sections.h2: When do Laclede County bills arrive and what are the ways to pay?
sections.html:
The office starts printing statements in late October, once the County Clerk delivers the tax books, and mails them in November. December 31 is the due date. Real estate and personal property arrive as two separate statements, and one check may cover both.

The counter is open from 8am to 4pm on weekdays and closes for state and federal holidays. Paying after December 31 means following the delinquency schedule printed on your statement, and the office is the place to ask for a penalty figure.

  • Walk in with cash, a personal check, a money order or a cashier's check
  • Mail a check in the return envelope and never include cash
  • Pay by card on the website or by telephone, with a convenience fee added
  • Use the drop box at the Second Street courthouse entrance, which takes payments at any hour

A paid receipt returns by mail after processing. A late payment dropped in the box without its penalty is sent back.

sections.h2: Can I spread the bill out or freeze it as a senior in Laclede County?
sections.html:
Yes to the first for most owners, and maybe to the second. The Collector offers a prepay plan of ten equal payments built from last year's tax, with the eleventh payment settling the remainder. Payments come out of a bank account automatically. Delinquent accounts and parcels paid through a lender's escrow cannot join, and the number to call is (417) 532-4301.

The senior credit locks the homestead real estate tax at the first-year amount. You may claim one home only, you must live in it, and you renew each year between April 1 and the last Friday in May. The first year always shows a credit of zero, because nothing is refunded for earlier years. The county's home page says the 2026 applications have closed.

The program is not an exemption, so the tax stays on the home. A seller who is enrolled should ask the collector what happens to the credit when the house changes hands.

sections.h2: What if I think my Laclede County value is too high?
sections.html:
Go to the Assessor first, then to the county board of equalization, then to the State Tax Commission. The board wants your appeal in by the second Monday in July. After its letter arrives, you have 30 days to go to the Commission.

You may dispute a value and still be current on the bill. The Commission's guidance says to send the full payment to the collector, mark it as a protest, and attach your written reasons and the market value you claim. A postmark of December 31 or earlier counts.

An estate, trust, LLC or corporation cannot file the Commission appeal without a lawyer. A person settling a relative's estate before a sale should keep that rule in mind.

sections.h2: What does a Laclede County tax certificate sale mean for the owner?
sections.html:
At the sale a bidder pays your back tax and receives a certificate, not a deed. It takes place on the fourth Monday in August at 10 a.m. at the courthouse, 200 N. Adams in Lebanon, after a newspaper lists the parcels for three weeks. Paying the taxes, penalty, interest and costs any time before the bidding keeps the property off the block.

A winning bidder walks away with a certificate of purchase. To redeem, the owner pays the certificate's base amount plus 10% annual interest, and adds any later tax the buyer paid with the same interest. The collector asks for a day's notice and suggests allowing 20 minutes.

After the year runs out, the holder can seek a collector's deed, but only after certified-mail notices to the owner and to lienholders at least 90 days earlier. Liens survive the sale itself. Bid money over the taxes and costs belongs to the owner of record.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Laclede County house that has back taxes?
sections.html:
Ask the collector for an exact payoff, give it to the title company, and let the closing pay it out of the price.

  • If you bought the house before October, the statement may have gone to the previous owner, so ask them and the collector.
  • If the August sale is close, pay the balance before that date.
  • Tell the collector about the sale if you use the installment plan or senior credit.
  • Call the Assessor about a wrong value well before July.

Written payoff figures protect you if the amount changes by the closing date.

faqs.q: Is the Laclede County property tax deadline December 31?
faqs.a: Yes. Statements arrive in November and are due December 31. Anything paid later follows the delinquency schedule on the statement.

faqs.q: Which office fixes an error in my Laclede County parcel record?
faqs.a: The Assessor, at (417) 532-7163. The collector cannot change a bill because it must collect from the assessor's records.

faqs.q: Can I pay Laclede County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Card payments work online or by phone and carry a convenience fee. The office also takes cash, checks and money orders, and there is a courthouse drop box.

faqs.q: When must I appeal a Laclede County value?
faqs.a: The county board of equalization needs your appeal by the second Monday in July. The State Tax Commission allows 30 days from the date of the board's letter.

faqs.q: Is it possible to close on a Laclede County home with back tax owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a written payoff from the collector so the title company can pay it from your proceeds. If the August sale is near, clearing the balance first keeps the parcel off the list.
